cim: Only 24% of Andorra's SMEs Use Artificial Intelligence in 2026
cim_eredeti: Only 24% of Andorra's SMEs Use Artificial Intelligence in 2026
szoveg_eredeti:
The adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is progressing at two different speeds in Andorra. While 100% of the Principality's large companies already use this technology, only 24% of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have incorporated it into their operations, according to the latest study on the country's digital divide.

This gap highlights the difficulties many small businesses face in taking advantage of AI applications in areas such as process automation, customer service and administrative management.

Jesús Almir, CEO of the digital marketing agency DigiAcción, believes that one of the main obstacles is a lack of understanding of AI's practical applications in business.

Although many companies have already experimented with tools such as ChatGPT, they still struggle to identify which tasks can be automated and which technological solutions best suit their needs.

Almir also warns that exaggerated promises from certain providers can create unrealistic expectations among business owners, particularly when these tools are presented as solutions capable of solving virtually any problem.

One Andorran company that has already integrated AI into its daily operations is Montpackers, a digital platform specialising in adventure tourism and mountain activities.

Its manager, Anton Òdena, explains that artificial intelligence has become a regular tool for developing and reviewing computer code, detecting errors, preparing meetings, drafting emails and managing customer information.

"With AI, it's as if one programmer could do the work of five," Òdena says, although he notes that productivity gains depend on the characteristics of each task.

The company has also developed its own system to centralise internal information and retrieve commercial data more quickly, reducing the time spent on certain administrative tasks.

These applications demonstrate that artificial intelligence is not limited to generating text or images. It can also be integrated into internal business processes to improve efficiency and everyday operations.

Meanwhile, Pol Guasch of Minerva Data Solutions highlights the potential of AI agents, systems capable of interacting with different digital tools and performing tasks automatically.

These solutions can help businesses manage processes that previously required constant human intervention.

However, Guasch warns that greater autonomy in AI systems must be accompanied by appropriate control and supervision mechanisms.

Among the main precautions are the need to establish limited permissions, control access to information and maintain human oversight, particularly when these tools handle sensitive data.

The objective is to take advantage of automation without compromising security or losing control over business operations.

Industry professionals identify numerous artificial intelligence applications that could benefit Andorra's small and medium-sized enterprises.

These include customer support outside business hours, automated email management, content creation, translations and data analysis.

Such tools can enable businesses with small teams to carry out certain tasks more quickly and dedicate more resources to higher-value activities.

Experts agree that companies failing to adapt to this technological transformation risk losing competitiveness to businesses that successfully automate processes, reduce costs and improve response times.

A lack of knowledge and specialised training therefore remains one of the main challenges to expanding artificial intelligence adoption among SMEs in the Principality.

Against this backdrop, Hotel Roc Blanc will host a new free Speakers' Corner session on November 30, focusing on the future of software development and the impact of artificial intelligence.

The event will explore the changes this technology is bringing to the business world and its potential applications.

The session comes at a time when the gap between large companies and SMEs in artificial intelligence adoption remains significant in Andorra.

While major companies have already incorporated AI tools into their operations, the challenge for smaller businesses will be to identify useful applications, acquire the necessary skills and benefit from the technology without taking unnecessary risks.
